text:
emily: Morning alert — payment-service started returning 401s around 08:18Z. Seeing lots of auth failures, stack shows 'invalid issuer'.
raj: Confirmed. 401 spike across several services. Sample log: "token validation failed: unexpected issuer 'redwood-legacy'"
micah: Any recent rotations or config pushes for token-service?
deploy-bot: key-rotation job finished at 2026-03-17T08:15Z (released kid=k2).
emily: That aligns. Could be a mismatch between minted tokens and auth validator expecting a new issuer.
raj: Quick repro:
```
TOKEN=<example_token_with_iss_redwood-legacy>
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/payments/charge
# -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"token issuer mismatch"}
```
micah: I can patch auth-validator to accept the legacy issuer as a short-term mitigation (dual-issuer mode). Prefer that over rolling token-service back immediately.
sre-oncall: Applying canary patch to auth-validator now, will enable legacy issuer acceptance for requests < 1h grace window.
sre-oncall: Canary deployed to 2/6 nodes; observed failure rate drop from ~18% to ~3% for affected routes.
emily: Notifying SRT and customers with degraded auth. Posting on status page: "Authentication errors for some service accounts — mitigation in progress." :warning:
raj: Root cause hypothesis: token-service config change altered the "iss" string during a staggered rollout. JWK rotation (kid -> k2) completed, but a subset of minting instances were still issuing tokens with the old issuer; validators reject them because issuer check is strict. Edge caching of /jwks with 300s TTL probably made things worse.
micah: Agreed. Two simultaneous factors: issuer string drift + partial jwks propagation -> signature/iss/aud checks failing intermittently.
emily: Short-term actions I pushed:
- enable dual-issuer acceptance in auth-validator (1h)
- invalidate CDN /jwks cache (purge)
- rollback token-service config in canary pool if still minting old issuer
- status update to customers

raj: For transparency: logs show ~420 affected requests between 08:15–08:40Z, mostly service-account tokens used by background jobs.
sre-oncall: Purged CDN cache and forced jwks fetches from all auth-validator nodes. Verified all nodes now report kid=k2 and have updated keyset.
deploy-bot: token-service rollback to previous config executed at 08:42Z for canary instances.
emily: Error rates back to baseline ~08:47Z. Raising incident ticket INC-8472 and scheduling a short postmortem.
micah: Postmortem recommendations (draft):
- require coordinated issuer + jwks rollout with a graceful dual-issuer acceptance window
- make key rotations emit a config-change event so minting services refresh issuer atomically
- set CDN TTL to 0 for /jwks during rotation or implement cache-busting headers
- add synthetic checks that validate minted tokens end-to-end after rotation

raj: Also add an alert for sudden issuer mismatch errors in logs (rate threshold) so we catch this earlier.
emily: Created INC-8472 and linked PRs for mitigation + postmortem notes. Marking incident as mitigated; will follow up with scheduled postmortem and action items. :white_check_mark:
